political_impact.text: The order turned the existing bureaus, such as the Geological Survey, Forest Service, Census and General Land Office, into the research arm of a commission that had no money or staff of its own.

Congress answered Roosevelt's unauthorized commissions with the Tawney amendment, which barred public money for any commission not authorized by law and barred lending department staff to one; the staff ban killed the National Conservation Commission.
political_impact.source: Act of March 4, 1909, ch. 299, sec. 9, 35 Stat. 945, 1027

political_impact.text: Roosevelt wrote that the amendment forbade him to appoint further commissions and that he would have refused to obey it had he stayed in office; the statute itself cut off money and staff rather than banning appointments.

legacy.text: The commission's three-volume Report, transmitted January 22, 1909, was in Roosevelt's words "the first inventory of its natural resources ever made by any nation."
legacy.source: S. Doc. No. 676, 60th Cong., 2d Sess.; Roosevelt's message of transmittal

legacy.text: Congress refused to fund the commission's continuation, but the report and the conference behind it shaped resource policy for decades.

political_impact.text: The Navy's Chief of Ordnance reported fuel-oil tank sets proposed on Woman Key and Man Key for the Key West station.
political_impact.source: Navy Department, Annual Reports, 1909, Miscellaneous Reports, p. 429

legacy.text: The naval reservation and Roosevelt's Key West bird reservation overlapped on paper for seventy-four years, until the naval claim was revoked after the 1975 wilderness designation.

today.name: Key West National Wildlife Refuge
today.note: When the naval reservation was revoked in 1982 the lands remained withdrawn for the refuge under Executive Order 923.

today.name: Florida Keys Wilderness
today.note: Man Key and Woman Key lie inside the congressionally designated wilderness.

related.note: The Key West bird reservation, which expressly left this naval reservation standing on the same two keys.

later_actions.text: Coolidge's Executive Order 4060 reserved for naval purposes all the islands, keys, harbors and shoals in a block of townships that included the two keys.
Congress designated the Florida Keys Wilderness, which takes in Man Key and Woman Key.
Public Land Order 6214 revoked Executive Order 808 and Executive Order 4060, leaving the lands withdrawn for the Key West National Wildlife Refuge.

uncertain: The exact wording of Executive Order 808 is not known; no printing has been found.

political_impact.text: The commission reported in February 1909 as Better Security of Life at Sea; the report makes no reference to the General Slocum disaster.

uncertain: Whether newspapers of 1908 linked the commission to the General Slocum disaster has not been checked.

political_impact.text: The pay order was part of the quiet drive for efficiency in the departments and drew little notice.

related.note: Applied the principles of the report of the Committee on Grades and Salaries, which EO 651 had created.

legacy.text: The Port Neuf name ended with this order; the old Port Neuf lands are today the Westside Ranger District of the Caribou-Targhee National Forest.
The Pocatello name was dropped in 1915, when that forest went into the Cache.

today.name: Caribou-Targhee National Forest (Westside Ranger District)
today.note: The former Port Neuf National Forest lands.

related.note: Signed the same day; the two orders together dissolved the Bear River National Forest.

later_actions.text: The Pocatello National Forest was merged into the Cache and its name discontinued.

uncertain: The exact wording of Executive Order 801 has not been checked; no transcription is available.

legacy.text: The Cache National Forest was never abolished; in 1973 its administration was split along the Utah–Idaho line.

today.name: Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest
today.note: The Utah four-fifths of the Cache, now the Logan and Ogden Ranger Districts; the Cache's principal successor.

today.name: Caribou-Targhee National Forest (Montpelier Ranger District)
today.note: The Idaho portion of the Cache.

related.note: Signed the same day; the two orders together dissolved the Bear River National Forest.

later_actions.text: The Cache's Utah portion was merged administratively with the Wasatch National Forest and its Idaho portion went to the Caribou.
The Wasatch-Cache joined the Uinta to form the Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest.
